issue_context.title: `bluesound_group` attribute only present in groups of two
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When I join one Bluesound node to the master, the following attribute appears in the state of both nodes:

    bluesound_group: ["Dining Room", "Kitchen"]

When I join a third node to the existing group, the attribute disappears.

Currently there is no way that I can see to determine whether a node is part of a group of more than two nodes.



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.11.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Bluesound

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/bluesound/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

Setting up a local dev environment is the easiest way I know.

But you don't have to do this. It would have been nice to have if it were no big hassle. I added tests for it, and I am optimistic that this should be fixed.

Finally managed to get a dev environment set up. Five years of retirement rots your brain...

This is almost working but there is still an issue. I have 4 bluesound amplifiers plus a NAD amplifier.

The state for the bluesound amps work correctly - the `bluesound_group` gets updated as I add or remove bluesound amps or the NAD amp.

The state for the NAD, however, is not updated correctly. When I add the NAD to a group, the `bluesound_group` reflects the state of that attribute before the NAD was added. eg if the group consisted of `diningroom, kitchen`, then I added `cine` (ie the NAD), then the attribute for the bluesound amps would be `diningroom, kitchen, cine` but for the NAD it would be `diningroom, kitchen`.

Unjoining a node other than NAD doesn't seem to update the NAD attribute, but unjoining the NAD removes that attribute from the NAD.

Hope this help - let me know if there is any more info I can provide you.

I have one idea for the cause. How long did you wait for ``bluesound_group` to update after you added the NAD Player to the group? It might be a timing issue depending on how the players communicate with each other. You could try to wait for 125 seconds and see if the bluesound_group is updated then.

If this doesn't work, knowing the player's `/SyncStatus` would be helpful. You would have to open `http://<player_ip>:11000/SyncStatus` with an HTTP Client of your choice (or Browser, Firefox works) while you have the problem. The master and the NAD player should be enough. And you might want to redact the MAC of your player before posting the response here.

You're right, I've noticed other inconsistencies, not just with the NAD amp. But they seem to resolve within about 125 seconds.

One node not knowing about the presence of another node in the group I can deal with, but it seems odd that a node which has just joined (and previously didn't possess a `bluesound_group` attribute) now does have the attribute but it doesn't include itself. 

```
SyncStatus of NAD

This XML file does not appear to have any style information associated with it. The document tree is shown below.

It’s the timing problem then. The SyncStatus is the source for which player belongs to which group. But only the master knows the whole group. The flow is:

- Slave player gets new SyncStatus. We know only the master at that point.
- We look at the last SyncStatus for the master to get the whole group.
- We set the slaves bluesound group based on the masters SyncStatus.(The last one that was received)

This works if the master is updated first, but if the slave is updated first the old master SyncStatus is used. (Which does not have the new member yet).

I will fix this, but I still have two other PRs which have to be merged first.
